newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Profuturo-GNP sees 16 pct market share.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Profuturo-GNP sees 16 pct market share.

text.p: Mexican pension management firm Afore Profuturo-GNP affiliated 1.68 million workers in the first quarter, though the paperwork on most of them has not been completed, a top company official said on Tuesday.
"We have affiliated 16 percent of the market, which puts us in third place," company director general Eduardo Silva Pylypciow told Reuters in an interview.
He did not say what the top two pension firms (Afores) were. Afore Bancomer and Afore Banamex had been expected to have the largest market shares in the early stages.

Some 10.5 million permenantly insured workers are eligible to join the private pension scheme, which was launched earlier this year, and the maximum market share that any Afore is allowed is 17 percent.
Silva Pylypciow said that 160,000 of the accounts had been passed on to Procesar, the system that processes pension accounts.
He said that number is low compared to the total number of workers who have signed up with Profuturo-GNP because many clients lack documents necessary to complete the paperwork.
"Many workers do not have the new Mexican Social Security Institute credential. We are helping them get it, but the process needs at least eight working days," he said.
Profuturo has 4,500 sales staff spread across 84 Mexican cities seeking to recruit workers.
It was set up by Mexican insurer Grupo Nacional Provincial, Chilean pension fund Provida and Spain's Banco Bilbao Vizcaya, with stakes of 51 percent, 24 percent and 25 percent, respectively.
